page: Google Cloud Platform a2-megagpu-16g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for massive parallel computing workloads. It features 16 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a total of 640 GB of VRAM, paired with 96 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The system includes 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. System memory is substantial at 1360.0 GB, yielding 14.17 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression/decompression, consistently fall into the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested systems. However, multi-core capabilities are robust, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU extended instructions testing in the strong category, representing the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also a key strength, with cached small-block and uncached large-block read operations both scoring in the top 25%. Other operations, including Passmark database tasks, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, perform in the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a high-density hardware class where the primary value lies in the massive GPU and memory allocation rather than raw single-threaded CPU speed. The main tradeoff is the weak single-core CPU performance and the complete lack of local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be provisioned. This server is best fit for highly parallelized workloads such as deep learning training, large-scale GPU-accelerated data science, and complex multi-threaded simulations that can leverage the 16 A100 GPUs and 1360 GB of system memory.
